how: Rendered the home screen from the app's own component: headline 'Good things, fair prices.', the line 'Donkey sells everyday goods chosen with care...' and a 'Sign up' button printed.
Rendered home: every 'Sign up' button calls the shop-entry action that opens the hosted sign-in page (login). No sign-up form exists in the app's source.
Rendered the How it works page with no written record: the Delivery panel printed "We'll add our delivery details here soon."
Rendered the Contact page with no written record: it printed 'Contact details are on their way. Check back soon.' and hid the detail cards.

check: T01 done-when: every top-menu page opens with the designs' words and a Sign up button
how: Rendered home, how it works, contact, products (empty) and about: each printed the designers' wording and at least one 'Sign up' button.

check: ED-01 AC2 visitor pages link nothing to /editor
how: Rendered every visitor page: no link or data-goto to /editor or /editor/sign-in appeared in any output (to /editor: false on all five).

text: The project's sign-up is off (public signup-settings reports email sign-up disabled), so the single Sign up button opens the hosted sign-in page without the create-account prompt; both Sign in and Sign up use one hosted page.
Email, phone and address are never starting content. With no record written the Contact page shows its empty line and the footer shows no contact details, as the designs' rules say.
Product photos have no file yet, so each product card shows the design's own picture placeholder (photo icon) rather than one invented image address.

how: Rendered the editors' area: a signed-in Editor sees the header menu with Products, Page wording and Form entries, the Editors panel with the invite form, and the products table. Screen renders from the app's own component.

Rendered every visitor page after the editors' area was added: home, how it works, about, contact and products printed no link to /editor (to /editor: false on all five). Only /editor/sign-in is reachable from the editors' side.

check: ED-01 role check reads the signed-in person's roles
how: Ran the area's own role reader with roles given as a plain list and grouped by company: editor list and grouped editor both open the area; no roles and a shopper company stay closed.

check: ED-01 invite sends the Editor role
how: Rendered the Editors panel: the invite form shows the email field and 'Send the invite'. Source sends the new account with roles: ["editor"] through the app's SDK client.

text: The Editor role may now list, invite and change people
The Editor role is the project's existing one, reused by name. Its people permissions were added; the project has companies off, so nothing to copy to other companies.

The project's mail is set up (a default mail configuration exists), so invite emails can go out. An editor who has no invite gets a plain 'This area is for the site's editors' page with a way back to the shop.
